snapshot.about: Larsen & Toubro Ltd is a multinational conglomerate which is primarily engaged in providing engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) solutions in key sectors such as Infrastructure, Hydrocarbon, Power, Process Industries and Defence, Information Technology and Financial Services in domestic and international markets.
key_points: a) Infrastructure Projects (47% in FY26 vs 51% in FY25):

The segment undertakes EPC activities across buildings and factories, transportation, heavy civil infrastructure, power transmission and distribution, renewable energy, water and effluent treatment, and minerals and metals sectors.

cash.note: Post-investment cash = CFO + CFI (screener doesn't split capex from treasury moves); treat as a proxy for FCF.

items.quote: Given the strength of our opportunity pipeline and the underlying market dynamics, we remain confident of achieving our order inflow growth guidance of 10% to 12% band for the current year.
items.speaker: Energy
items.why: Revenue YoY +15.8% on average (Sep 2026) vs 10–12% promised — 1 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: Factoring in the expected utilizati on of customer advances and increased vendor payments as the execution accelerates in H2, we are maintaining our FY '27 working capital guidance of around 10%.
items.speaker: Energy
items.why: Loan growth isn't in the quarterly P&L — AUM/loan book is in the investor presentation.

items.quote: Concluding with the Lakshya guidance, over the next five years, we are targeting order inflow growth at a CAGR return of 10% to 12%, revenue growth of 12% to 15%, and a Return on Equity in the range of 16% to 17%.
items.speaker: P. Ramakrishnan
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.2% on average (Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 10–12% promised — 2 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: But as you see, when I talked in the last part of my speech, I did say that we are taking ourselves a target of 12% to 15% Revenue CAGR over the L31 plan, which obviously means that it also factors the fact that FY28 onwards the revenue growth momentum should get stabilized, assuming external condition and all other things remaining favourable.
items.speaker: P. Ramakrishnan
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.2% on average (Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 12–15% promised — 2 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: So when I'm giving the guidance of 16% to 17%, if you just add up the numbers of the investment that we are talking about, be it Electronics, be it Green Energy, be it Data Center, , the 12% to 15% revenue growth is all coming from what you call largely PPM and the ITTS portfolio.
items.speaker: P. Ramakrishnan
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.2% on average (Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 16–17% promised — 2 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: The economic growth in India for FY '27 is expected to be around 6.9%, supported by resilient household demand, sustained public capital expenditure, and continued strength in the services sector.
items.speaker: P. Ramakrishnan
items.why: Capex isn't in the quarterly P&L — check the next annual report.

items.quote: Basis the 9-month performance and the healthy prospects pipeline for the near term, we will be exceeding the 10% order inflow guidance for FY '26.
items.speaker: Sensitivity
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.3% on average (Mar 2026, Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 10% promised — 3 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: We expect the customary ramp -up in project execution during Q4 and are reasonably confident of achieving our full year revenue growth guidance of 15%.
items.speaker: Sensitivity
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.3% on average (Mar 2026, Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 15% promised — 3 of 4 quarters in.

items.quote: So Sumit, just to add, I did emphasize that the margin guidance of 8.5% remains the effort for taking into account that we have had a good 9 months despite the fact of Hydrocarbon margins having moved southwards this year.
items.speaker: P. Ramakrishnan
items.why: Operating margin averaged 12.0% in the 3 quarters since (guided 8.5%).

items.quote: The global economy is entering calendar 2026 with growth expected to remain modest at roughly the 3% range.
items.speaker: Sensitivity
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.3% on average (Mar 2026, Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 3% promised.

items.quote: We are confident of ex ceeding our full year FY '26 guidance of 10% growth in group order inflows for the current year.
items.speaker: Sensitivity
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.1% on average (Dec 2025, Mar 2026, Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 10% promised.

items.quote: Accordingly, we maintain our full year revenue growth guidance at 15%.
items.speaker: Sensitivity
items.why: Revenue YoY +11.1% on average (Dec 2025, Mar 2026, Jun 2026, Sep 2026) vs 15% promised.

items.quote: With the execution momentum expected to pick up in H2, we are reasonably confident to achieve our full year EBITDA margin target of 8.5%.
items.speaker: Sensitivity

items.quote: 7% of the total order book , and there are projects which are related to the Jal Jeevan Mission project and once the allocations of the government start coming in, we do expect the execution momentum to smoothen out in the subsequent quarters.

promises.read: 9 of 12 checkable promises met or on track; analysts kept pressing on margins.

bull: Revenue compounding 16.0% a year over 3 years (steady vs 16.0% 5-yr).
Management delivered 9 of 12 checkable guidance points over the last 4 calls.
bear: Margins compressing: 13.3% avg over last 3 yrs vs 16.0% before.
Working-capital cycle lengthening — cash getting tied up.
